instruction: Model a Hammer with ShadowBox (Mask 3 Views) + DynaMesh Clean The opened `scene.obj` contains a ZBrush Tool with three SubTools that define the three orthographic silhouettes of a target hammer shape: - SilhouetteFront: a flat polygon in the XY plane (at z=0) showing the hammer's front view - a long thin vertical rectangle (handle) with a wide horizontal rectangle at its top (the head). - SilhouetteSide: a flat polygon in the YZ plane (at x=0) showing the hammer's side view - a thinner profile for the handle and a slightly thicker head. - SilhouetteTop: a flat polygon in the XZ plane (at y=0.92, the head height) showing the top-down view of the head. These silhouettes are provided as reference; they are not themselves the output. Your task is to use ShadowBox to produce the 3D hammer shape whose three-view projection matches the silhouettes. Export the Hammer SubTool as `C:\Users\user\Desktop\output.obj`. The exported `C:\Users\user\Desktop\output.obj` must satisfy: - Exactly one SubTool, named Hammer. - The mesh is manifold (every edge shared by exactly two faces). - The SubTool's axis-aligned bounding box is approximately 0.5 x 2.0 x 0.3 BU (handle longer than head is wide/deep), each dimension within 20% tolerance. - The XY-plane silhouette of the Hammer (its front-view projection) overlaps the SilhouetteFront polygons with Intersection-over-Union at least 0.5. - The SubTool carries at most 6 polygroups (ShadowBox + DynaMesh naturally produces a small number of polygroups).

command: import pyautogui, time; time.sleep(20); pyautogui.press('enter'); time.sleep(1); pyautogui.press('enter'); time.sleep(5)
